profile.name: FOMC Member Speaks
profile.what: Remarks from a regional Fed president or governor.
profile.why_gold: Mostly background, but a known hawk turning dovish - or the reverse - is a genuine signal, and voting members matter more than non-voters.
profile.watch: Whether the speaker votes this year, and whether they are departing from their usual stance.
profile.gotchas: Several speakers a day is normal and almost always noise. Treat as background unless the tone genuinely shifts.

profile.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
profile.what: Survey of purchasing managers. Above 50 means expansion. Released 15:00 UK.
profile.who: Institute for Supply Management, first business day of the month
profile.why_gold: A timely growth signal that arrives before the hard data. Weakness feeds recession pricing, which is usually gold-supportive.
profile.watch: The prices-paid and new-orders sub-indices carry more information than the headline.
profile.gotchas: Manufacturing is a small share of US output, so the survey overstates its own importance.

profile.name: JOLTS Job Openings
profile.what: Job openings, hires and quits. Released 15:00 UK, roughly six weeks in arrears.
profile.why_gold: The vacancy-to-unemployed ratio is a labour-tightness gauge the Fed has cited directly.
profile.watch: The quits rate, as a measure of worker confidence.
profile.gotchas: Very stale by release, and the response rate has been falling for years.
